label: EltonTraits 1.0: species-level foraging attributes of the world's birds and mammals (Wilman et al. 2014)
governance: Ecological Society of America data paper (Wilman et al. 2014, Ecology 95:2027, Ecological Archives E095-178; DOI resolves, checked 2026-10-31). The ESA archive states no licence. The Wiley figshare deposit of the same archive (article 3559887, 'Data Paper. Data Paper', version 1, published 2016-08-10) is licensed CC0 and lists BirdFuncDat.txt (file 5631081, md5 d6197b2cd90ca3ece0a7393abbf8b7fc) and MamFuncDat.txt (file 5631084, md5 59c3eee29d3ed0a33a002975a5a8cc75).
versioning: Single frozen release, version 1.0 (2014). BirdFuncDat.txt: 9,993 species rows with a scientific name (the data paper's 9,993 birds); file also contains trailing citation/blank lines and quoted fields with embedded newlines, so naive line counts give 10,011, 10,203 or 10,205. MamFuncDat.txt: 5,400 species rows (5,403 pandas rows including three trailing non-data lines). Identical bytes are served by esapubs and by figshare.
known_issues: Row-count artefacts in vendored records: bird counts 10,011 / 10,203 / 10,205 / 9,995 and mammal count 5,403 are line counts, not species rows; the correct species counts are 9,993 birds and 5,400 mammals (re-derived 2026-10-31 from both esapubs and figshare copies, checksums matched).
Mammal body masses are taken from PanTHERIA, so EltonTraits is not independent of that vendored source.
MamFuncDat.txt has no order column; order-level counts (e.g. Cetacea = 84) cannot be re-derived from the file alone.
Licence 'CC BY 4.0 (figshare deposit)' in one vendored record is wrong: the figshare record is CC0; esapubs states no licence.
The esapubs directory answers HTTP 403 to scripts; the files themselves download.
rationale: Peer-reviewed data paper with a registered DOI, a frozen version and a CC0 mirror justify high authority. Independence is scored 0.5 because EltonTraits is a compilation whose mammal body-mass values are ingested from PanTHERIA (also vendored here) and whose bird data derive from handbook sources. Authenticity is high: both files re-downloaded from esapubs and figshare match the recorded SHA-256 values exactly and the data paper's bird species total is reproduced.
